findings.issue_text: [BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-69 — The downsize loop caps at 5 iterations of 80% geometry (~0.8⁵ ≈ 33% linear reduction), and ImageMagick file-size does not shrink proportionally with geometry for many formats — a very large image that stays above max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts is passed to Upload.create_for oversized, returning a 'file too large' validation error — the exact failure this feature exists to eliminate still occurs for the largest images, with no retry or user-facing indication that downsizing was attempted and gave up.

[BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) reads and writes the same tempfile path; ImageMagick convert with identical input/output paths can truncate the source while streaming it, and convert_with returns false on nonzero exit status which the controller ignores entirely — a failed convert (corrupt file, ImageMagick missing, bad geometry) leaves the loop silently spinning 5 times or leaves a truncated/corrupt tempfile that Upload.create_for processes as a 0-byte or broken image.

[ADVISORY] app/models/optimized_image.rb:146-157 — downsize is defined twice in a row; the first definition is immediately dead code shadowed by the second definition taking a raw dimensions string — the next reader/edit changes the first definition believing it's live (e.g. adding allow_animation handling or validation there) and the change has zero effect; also the two definitions have different arities so a caller argument-count mistake silently resolves to the wrong one. The first 4-line def should be deleted.

[ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 and app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — Both the client-side max-size check and FileHelper.download's size cap are hardcoded to 10MB/10.megabytes, discarding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb entirely — an admin who sets max_image_size_kb below 10240 gets uploads blocked client-side at 10MB that the server then downsizes anyway (inconsistent UX), and for attachments the server-side Upload.create_for limit is still the SiteSetting, so files between the SiteSetting and 10MB pass the client check and fail on the server with a generic error.

[BUG] app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 — `downsize` is defined twice in the same class body (arity-5 `width, height` version followed by `dimensions` string version); the second silently replaces the first, making the first dead code and the signature ambiguous — a maintenance trap where the next edit targets the wrong definition.

[BUG] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side image size gate is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB, deleting the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`-based validation; for non-image types the client now claims 10240 KB is fine, user uploads 9 MB, transfers it fully, and the server rejects it.

[BUG] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 error path hardcodes `10 * 1024` as the reported max even though the server rejects at `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, which admins may set above or below 10 MB, producing a misleading alert about the actual limit.

[BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of 80% scaling (0.8^5 ≈ 0.33), so a file just over 3× the limit can exit the loop still oversized and fall through to `Upload.create_for` with a generic 'file too large' error; there is no post-loop check or fallback error, and highly compressed images (e.g., solid-color PNG) may not shrink at all, wasting 5 shell invocations silently.

[BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — The downsize gate uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` based on client-supplied/URL-derived filename without content-type verification; after downsizing, the preserved filename/content_type means a non-GIF-named animated file takes the non-animated instruction path and drops animation frames silently, converting the user's animated upload to a still with no warning.

[ADVISORY] Whole diff — No tests anywhere for the new server-side downsize loop (loop bound, animation preservation, oversized-after-retry) or the changed `optimize`/`downsize` signatures; the deleted `dimensions()` helper and changed signature affect every existing call site, so a regression in avatar/thumbnail resizing would ship unverified.

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:68 — The new processing path is gated on `max_image_size_kb > 0` and `allow_animated_thumbnails`, bypassing the parallel `allow_animated_avatars`/animated-image handling in `OptimizedImage`; users on sites that allow animated avatars but not animated thumbnails get their avatar silently flattened.
[BUG] utilities.js:182 removes admin-configured SiteSettings max size limits by hardcoding 10 * 1024, breaking enforcement of client-side upload size limits for all upload types
[BUG] utilities.js:246 413 handler shows users a hardcoded 10MB limit in the error message instead of the actual configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb

[BUG] uploads_controller.rb:55 API URL-download path replaces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes with hardcoded 10.megabytes download cap, removing admins' ability to bound remote download size for all API uploads including non-images

[BUG] optimized_image.rb:142-148 defines def self.downsize twice; Ruby silently redefines so the first definition is dead code and old 4-argument callers bind args incorrectly to the surviving signature, producing broken ImageMagick commands or TypeErrors

[ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:64-69 downsize loop passes "80%" as dimensions, and animation dispatch keys off .GIF extension which tempfile paths lack, so allow_animation never triggers and animated GIFs are silently flattened to a single frame; also 5 iterations of 80% shrink can leave only-modestly-oversized files still over-limit, failing Upload.create_for

[ADVISORY] utilities.js:182 client 10MB ceiling applies uniformly to all upload types while server downsizing only fires for images, so non-image files between the old setting and 10MB pass the client gate but are rejected server-side — client and server contracts now disagree

[ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:64 server-side downsize mutates the user's uploaded tempfile in place before Upload.create_for with no backup, so the original is destroyed if upload fails and sha/dedup semantics key off the downsized derivative rather than the original upload

[BUG] `def self.downsize` defined twice in the same class body; the second definition silently replaces the first, so every pre-existing 4-argument numeric caller misroutes: width binds to `dimensions` and height binds to `opts`, producing instructions computed from a bare "100" instead of "100x200" and `opts[:allow_animation]` evaluated on an Integer (always nil), breaking existing thumbnail downsize sites in post-processing and avatar generation.

[BUG] Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` breaks per-type, per-site configuration: sites with limits above 10MB block uploads client-side at 10MB, sites with lower limits let files through that the server rejects, and the error message reports "10240 KB" regardless of the real setting.

[BUG] `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` hardcodes the download cap, replacing `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, so the API URL-fetch path no longer respects the site setting in either direction and operators cannot change it without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] The downsize retry loop caps at 5 attempts with no check afterward; if the file is still over `max_image_size_kb` after 5 rounds (e.g. poor PNG recompression or convert command failure leaving the file untouched), `Upload.create_for` proceeds and fails with a generic error instead of the specific `file_too_large` message.

[ADVISORY] The in-place downsize loop runs before `Upload.create_for` for all image uploads, including types like avatars where the quality reduction was never part of the contract, unconditionally invoking an external `convert` subprocess up to 5 times on the request hot path, adding per-upload latency and re-encoding animated images per the unrelated `allow_animated_thumbnails` setting with no way to tune or disable it.

[BUG] The URL-download path replaces the admin-configured cap SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes with a hardcoded 10.megabytes, so remote fetches are no longer bounded by the admin setting, creating a bandwidth/disk/DoS vector.

[ADVISORY] The client check in utilities.js hardcodes 10 * 1024 and the 413 handler hardcodes 10 MB, discarding Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb, causing client-side limit drift from the server-enforced limit (broken UX and mismatched advertised vs enforced limits).

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs up to 5 convert invocations unconditionally with linear 80% scaling, wasting CPU on oversized images (10 MB only reaches ~3.3 MB after 5 attempts) and enabling CPU/memory amplification including decompression-bomb-style images that pass the byte-size cap but expand into huge raster work inside convert.
[ADVISORY] The downsize path is gated on FileHelper.is_image?(filename) alone, which trusts a client/URL-controlled filename, so any file named .png reaches the shell pipeline.
[ADVISORY] When convert_with fails (exitstatus != 0), the loop still burns all 5 attempts on a file that never shrinks.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize uses the same tempfile path as both ImageMagick input and output, which can truncate/corrupt the file mid-operation; tempfile.size is then re-read from the possibly corrupt file and passed to Upload.create_for, persisting corrupted uploads instead of a clean error.

[BUG] optimized_image.rb:144 — downsize is defined twice in the same module; the second definition silently overrides the first, so pre-existing 4-argument callers passing max_width/max_height have their arguments shifted into the dimensions parameter, producing broken ImageMagick instructions or ArgumentErrors on all pre-existing call sites; the duplicate definition should be deleted, keeping one signature and migrating old callers

[ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:64-70 — the new downsizing loop's failure path is silently swallowed: when OptimizedImage.downsize returns false the loop re-reads an unchanged tempfile.size five times, burns 5 wasted ImageMagick invocations, and falls through to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized file, yielding a misleading generic 'file too large' error with no debugging signal; no specs cover the downsize-failure path or iteration cap

[ADVISORY] utilities.js:182 — the client check hardcodes 10 * 1024 while the server uses SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so three hardcoded literals (utilities.js lines 182 and 246, uploads_controller.rb line 55) must be updated in lockstep; there is no single source of truth and no spec asserting client and server limits agree, risking future client/server limit divergence

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize overwrites the original uploaded file in place with a re-encoded lossy version, looping up to 5 times and compounding quality degradation with no backup, so the user's original image is irreversibly destroyed and if the size check still fails, the mangled file is submitted anyway and loses both the upload and the original quality for nothing.

[BUG] The loop has no exit check on downsize success: OptimizedImage.downsize returns false when the convert command fails, but the return value is ignored, so a failed convert leaves the loop re-running against the unchanged file 5 times before uploading the over-size or partially-written corrupt file.

[ADVISORY] When from == to, ImageMagick reading and writing the same file in one command can truncate the input before it's fully read (classic in-place convert hazard), producing a 0-byte or corrupt upload; the downsize(to:) API already supports writing to a sibling temp path but doesn't use it.

[ADVISORY] Two consecutive def self.downsize definitions exist in the same module after the diff: the two-arg version is silently redefined by the one-dimensional version, so existing callers passing width/height separately bind the height Integer to dimensions and produce malformed instructions; the dead first definition should be removed.

[ADVISORY] The resize/downsize refactor changes the shared API contract from (width, height) to a single dimensions string in one step with no expand phase, so out-of-tree/plugin callers still passing two integers generate malformed geometry like '300x' or fail with no error at load.

[BUG] `self.downsize` is defined twice in optimized_image.rb; the second definition (dimensions string) shadows the first (max_width/max_height args), breaking existing callers with TypeError and leaving dead shadowed code
[BUG] Hardcoded 10MB cap in utilities.js applies to all upload types, not just images, rejecting legitimate uploads above 10240KB and removing operator configurability of the client-side limit
[BUG] The 413 handler always reports 'max size 10MB' regardless of the server's actual enforced limit, causing users to retry still-too-large files in an unsatisfiable loop

[ADVISORY] The downsizing loop ignores `convert_with`'s return value, so corrupt/unreadable images cause 5 silent shell failures with no logging and a misleading 'file too large' error instead of the actual imagemagick failure

[ADVISORY] The in-place downsizing loop uses a fixed 80% for max 5 iterations, so very large images still exceed the limit after ~33% reduction, while 5 unbounded sequential imagemagick re-encodes run on the request thread with no timeout, amplifying CPU/latency for API uploads

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-69 — The downsize loop caps at 5 iterations of 80% geometry (~0.8⁵ ≈ 33% linear reduction), and ImageMagick file-size does not shrink proportionally with geometry for many formats — a very large image that stays above max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts is passed to Upload.create_for oversized, returning a 'file too large' validation error — the exact failure this feature exists to eliminate still occurs for the largest images, with no retry or user-facing indication that downsizing was attempted and gave up.

adjudication.rationale: The added block in `uploads_controller.rb` tries up to 5 downsizes (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`). If the file is still above the limit after 5 iterations, the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with an oversized `tempfile.size`, so the existing size validation can still fail and the user will just see the usual 'file too large' error. This is a real, diff-grounded edge case / incomplete handling rather than a clearly verifiable defect (it improves behavior for many cases but doesn’t guarantee success or provide explicit feedback when downsizing gives up).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) reads and writes the same tempfile path; ImageMagick convert with identical input/output paths can truncate the source while streaming it, and convert_with returns false on nonzero exit status which the controller ignores entirely — a failed convert (corrupt file, ImageMagick missing, bad geometry) leaves the loop silently spinning 5 times or leaves a truncated/corrupt tempfile that Upload.create_for processes as a 0-byte or broken image.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the controller calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (same input/output path) and not checking the return value of `downsize/optimize/convert_with`, so conversion failures would be silently ignored and the loop will just decrement attempts. However, the claim that ImageMagick will truncate/corrupt the file when input==output is not verifiable from the diff alone (it depends on external tool behavior), and the diff doesn’t prove `Upload.create_for` will accept/process a 0-byte file rather than error. This is a concrete robustness concern introduced by the change, but not a definitively provable defect from the diff itself.

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb the diff leaves two `self.downsize` definitions in the same class body: one taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and a later one taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later method silently overwrites the earlier, making the first dead code and changing call semantics; any existing callers still passing width/height would now be misinterpreted (4th arg becomes `opts`, leading to errors when accessed as a hash).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side image size gate is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB, deleting the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`-based validation; for non-image types the client now claims 10240 KB is fine, user uploads 9 MB, transfers it fully, and the server rejects it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows client-side size validation in `utilities.js` changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (per-type, server-configured) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB for all upload types, and similarly hardcodes 10MB for HTTP 413 handling. This can desync the client-side gate from actual server limits/settings (including non-image types that previously used `max_<type>_size_kb`), allowing users to attempt larger uploads than permitted and only fail after transfer/server-side checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 error path hardcodes `10 * 1024` as the reported max even though the server rejects at `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, which admins may set above or below 10 MB, producing a misleading alert about the actual limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces use of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` in the 413 handler with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). Since the server-side code still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (e.g., the new resize loop in `uploads_controller.rb` downsizes until under that setting), the client can now report a fixed 10MB limit even when the effective configured limit differs, making the alert potentially misleading. This mismatch is directly shown by the removal of the setting in JS and continued use of the setting on the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of 80% scaling (0.8^5 ≈ 0.33), so a file just over 3× the limit can exit the loop still oversized and fall through to `Upload.create_for` with a generic 'file too large' error; there is no post-loop check or fallback error, and highly compressed images (e.g., solid-color PNG) may not shrink at all, wasting 5 shell invocations silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new downsize loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that runs at most 5 times with a fixed "80%" reduction (`attempt = 5` / `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...` / `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`). There is no explicit post-loop check or alternate handling if the file remains above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so the request will just proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` and rely on downstream validation/errors. This is an incomplete edge-case/UX/performance concern (extra shell invocations with no guarantee of success), but the diff does not show that an oversized upload would be incorrectly accepted, so it’s not a verifiable correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — The downsize gate uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` based on client-supplied/URL-derived filename without content-type verification; after downsizing, the preserved filename/content_type means a non-GIF-named animated file takes the non-animated instruction path and drops animation frames silently, converting the user's animated upload to a still with no warning.

adjudication.rationale: The new pre-upload downsize loop in `uploads_controller.rb` is gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` using the URL-/client-derived filename, not a verified content type. More importantly, it calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`, but `OptimizedImage.optimize` decides whether to use animated instructions based on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (i.e., the *tempfile path* extension). Tempfile paths commonly lack a `.gif` suffix, so an actually-animated GIF can be processed via the non-animated path, potentially dropping animation frames with no warning. This is a behavior/data-loss risk introduced by the new downsize step.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Whole diff — No tests anywhere for the new server-side downsize loop (loop bound, animation preservation, oversized-after-retry) or the changed `optimize`/`downsize` signatures; the deleted `dimensions()` helper and changed signature affect every existing call site, so a regression in avatar/thumbnail resizing would ship unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior (a bounded retry loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` until size <= `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`) and refactors `OptimizedImage.optimize`/`downsize` to take a single `dimensions` string (also removing the `dimensions()` helper). This kind of logic/signature change is regression-prone (loop termination, oversized-after-retries, animation option propagation, and any existing callers of `optimize`/`downsize`), and the diff itself includes no corresponding test additions to exercise these paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:68 — The new processing path is gated on `max_image_size_kb > 0` and `allow_animated_thumbnails`, bypassing the parallel `allow_animated_avatars`/animated-image handling in `OptimizedImage`; users on sites that allow animated avatars but not animated thumbnails get their avatar silently flattened.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsizing loop runs for any image upload (`FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`) and calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, animated handling is only used when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true; otherwise a `.GIF` will take the non-animated instruction path, which commonly flattens/loses animation. Because the controller hard-codes `allow_animated_thumbnails` for all uploads (not per upload type), this can incorrectly strip animation for uploads where animation should be allowed under a different setting (the finding’s avatar-specific scenario is plausible but not fully verifiable from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] utilities.js:182 removes admin-configured SiteSettings max size limits by hardcoding 10 * 1024, breaking enforcement of client-side upload size limits for all upload types

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces use of admin-configured `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` (and similarly hardcodes `max_image_size_kb` handling for HTTP 413). This removes per-type and site-configured client-side size enforcement shown in the original code, so admins’ configured limits no longer control the client-side upload checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] utilities.js:246 413 handler shows users a hardcoded 10MB limit in the error message instead of the actual configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the 413 handler was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the error message will always report 10MB even if `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` is configured to a different value, so the displayed limit can be incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] uploads_controller.rb:55 API URL-download path replaces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes with hardcoded 10.megabytes download cap, removing admins' ability to bound remote download size for all API uploads including non-images

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb, the API URL-download path changes the download size limit from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This directly removes the admin-configurable bound for remote downloads via `max_image_size_kb` and changes behavior for all API URL uploads (it’s not conditioned on file type there).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] optimized_image.rb:142-148 defines def self.downsize twice; Ruby silently redefines so the first definition is dead code and old 4-argument callers bind args incorrectly to the surviving signature, producing broken ImageMagick commands or TypeErrors

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb the diff leaves an earlier `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then introduces a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` later. In Ruby, the later definition silently overwrites the former, making the 4-argument version dead code. Any existing callers passing 4 args (from,to,width,height) will now bind `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` (an Integer), and `optimize` subsequently does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will raise (NoMethodError/TypeError) or generate incorrect ImageMagick instructions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] uploads_controller.rb:64-69 downsize loop passes "80%" as dimensions, and animation dispatch keys off .GIF extension which tempfile paths lack, so allow_animation never triggers and animated GIFs are silently flattened to a single frame; also 5 iterations of 80% shrink can leave only-modestly-oversized files still over-limit, failing Upload.create_for

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new shrink loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In optimized_image.rb, animated handling is selected only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is a tempfile path (typically without the original `.gif` extension), so `_animated` instructions will not be chosen even when `allow_animation` is true—likely causing animated GIFs to be processed as non-animated. Also, the loop hard-stops after 5 attempts even if `tempfile.size` remains over `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so `Upload.create_for(...)` can still fail for very large images despite the comment claiming automatic reduction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] utilities.js:182 client 10MB ceiling applies uniformly to all upload types while server downsizing only fires for images, so non-image files between the old setting and 10MB pass the client gate but are rejected server-side — client and server contracts now disagree

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the client-side size check is changed from the per-type site setting (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all upload types. On the server, the new automatic downsizing logic in `uploads_controller.rb` only runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` and compares against `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, meaning non-image uploads are still governed by whatever server-side limits exist (and are not reduced).
